title: Coherent normalization quotient and its exact singular support
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $X$ a reduced finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] whose irreducible components all have dimension one [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be the componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Let $N\subseteq X$ be the set of points $x$ such that $A_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and put $C_x=(
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u})_x$. The canonical map $\mathcal O_X	o
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u}$ is injective, its sheaf cokernel $Q$ fits into
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X\longrightarrow
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u}\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow0,$$
and all three modules are coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. For every $x$, the quotient identification $Q_x=C_x/A_x$ is canonical and finite as an $A_x$-module, and
$$Q_x=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in N.$$
The set $N$ is dense open and is exactly the smooth locus of $X	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Thus $\operatorname{Supp}Q=\{x:Q_x
e0\}=X\setminus N$ is a finite set of closed points and contains no generic point of an irreducible component. At every closed point $x$ the local ring $A_x$ is reduced Noetherian of Krull dimension one (the longest strict chain of prime ideals has length one), is essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], and the structural map $k	o\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism. The empty scheme is allowed, with $Q=0$ and empty support.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-normalization-affine-stalk-closure] to the reduced finite-type scheme $X$. It gives Noetherianness of $X$ and $X^
u$, the finite normalization, the dense open normal locus $N$, and its affine and stalk descriptions. In particular, on every affine open the structural map is the inclusion $R\hookrightarrow T$ into its finite integral closure. These inclusions imply injectivity of the sheaf map: a section in its kernel restricts to zero on an affine covering, hence is zero by the sheaf axiom. Write $B=
u_*\mathcal O_{X^
u}$ and define $Q=\operatorname{Coker}(\mathcal O_X	o B)$.

The structure sheaf of each of the two Noetherian schemes is quasi-coherent of finite type (locally it is the module $R$ generated by $1$), hence coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent] to the finite morphism $\nu$ and $\mathcal O_{X^\nu}$; thus $B$ is coherent. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth], its cokernel $Q$ is coherent. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact], the injective map and its cokernel give the asserted short exact sequence and the canonical isomorphism $Q_x=C_x/A_x$. The finite generating set of $C_x$ supplied by [lem-trf-normalization-affine-stalk-closure] maps to a finite generating set of $Q_x$.

proof.text: Use the structural inclusion $A_x\subseteq C_x\subseteq Q(A_x)=\prod_{i=1}^t K_i$ of [lem-trf-normalization-affine-stalk-closure], where $C_x$ is the integral closure. If $A_x$ is a normal domain, then $Q(A_x)$ is its fraction field and $C_x=A_x$ by the definition of integral closedness, so $Q_x=0$. Conversely, $Q_x=0$ implies $C_x=A_x$. Every coordinate idempotent of $\prod_iK_i$ satisfies the monic equation $e^2-e=0$, so belongs to $C_x=A_x$. In a local ring an idempotent is $0$ or $1$: one of $e,1-e$ is a unit and $e(1-e)=0$. Since $A_x$ is nonzero, $t\ge1$; if $t>1$ a coordinate idempotent is neither $0$ nor $1$, a contradiction. Thus $t=1$, so $A_x$ embeds in a field and is a domain; its integral closedness in that field says it is a normal domain. This proves $Q_x=0\iff x\in N$.

source.place: Tag 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal), coordinate-idempotent argument; specialized to a local ring using the explicit fraction-product description.

proof.text: A strict chain of irreducible closed subsets lies in an irreducible component. Since each component has dimension one, $\dim X\le1$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], $X$ is $T_0$ and every irreducible closed subset has its generic point. A point is either a component generic point or closed: if its closure is properly contained in a component and properly contains another nonempty irreducible closed subset, the resulting chain has length two. At a closed point $x$, [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] with $O=X,n=1$ gives $\dim_xX=1$; on a finite-type affine chart, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring] then gives $\dim A_x=1$. The affine and stalk models in [lem-trf-normalization-affine-stalk-closure] give reduced Noetherianness and $A_x=R_{\mathfrak p}$ for a finite-type $k$-algebra $R$, which is essentially of finite type by [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Since $x$ is closed in its affine chart, [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing](1) identifies its residue field with $k$ via the structural map.

source.place: Tag 0B1B (item-dimension-irreducibles-passing-through); algebra.tex Tag 00OU (lemma-dimension-closed-point-finite-type-field), Nullstellensatz Tag 00FV; schemes.tex Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: At a component generic point, [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field] shows that the local ring is a field, hence normal and regular (its zero maximal ideal is generated by zero elements). At every other point of $N$, Step 4 gives dimension one, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-dim-one-iff-normal] gives regularity. The open subscheme $N$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], and therefore regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. An algebraically closed field is perfect: an element algebraic over it has a linear minimal polynomial, so every algebraic extension is trivial. Apply [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth] to $N\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is locally of finite type by restriction of the finite-type affine charts. Hence every point of $N$ is smooth. Conversely a smooth point has a smooth open neighbourhood; [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] and [rem-pc-regular-normal](1) make its local ring normal. Thus $N$ is exactly the smooth locus.

By Step 3 the support is $Z=X\setminus N$, a closed subset since $N$ is open by Step 1. It misses every component generic point by Step 5. If $Z$ had a positive-length chain of irreducible closed subsets, its largest member would be properly contained in a component of $X$ (otherwise its generic point would lie in $Z$), producing a chain of length at least two in $X$, contrary to Step 4. Thus $\dim Z\le0$. The underlying space of the Noetherian scheme $X$ (Step 1) is a Noetherian topological space by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], and it is $T_0$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]: distinct points have distinct closures, since each irreducible closed set has a unique generic point. Hence [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-closed-finite] applied to the Noetherian $T_0$ space $X$ shows that $Z$ is finite and all its points are closed in $X$. If $X$ is empty, its structure sheaf and normalization pushforward are zero, so $Q=0$; all pointwise assertions are vacuous and the support is empty.
